rationale: The route uses 'Finite-product orthogonality' for this bounded lattice model; the finite-box endpoint supplies an 'induced finite graph' exactly, so no infinite-volume cutoff extrapolation is needed.
from_statement: Unproved-input proof route for iid Uniform[1,2] undirected nearest-neighbor Z^2 FPP, T_n=T(0,n e1). Refresh every edge independently at rate one. Let C_n(t)=Cov(T_n(W),T_n(W^t)) and H_n(t)=-C_n'(t). Finite-product orthogonality proves H_n>=0, H_n decreasing, Var(T_n)=integral_0^infinity H_n(t)dt and H_n(0)<=2n. If, for every epsilon in (0,1/3) and all large n, H_n(n^(-1/3-epsilon))>=c_epsilon n and C_n(n^(-1/3+epsilon))<=C_epsilon n^(2/3+epsilon), with positive constants independent of n, then c_epsilon n^(2/3-epsilon)<=Var(T_n)<=(2+C_epsilon)n^(2/3+epsilon), yielding variance exponent 1/3. BOTH crossover bounds remain unproved. The conditional implication awaits independent w365 review. Product structure and a linear geodesic-length bound alone only give order n; no parent solution or novelty is claimed.
to_statement: For every configuration of edge costs in [1,2] on the undirected nearest-neighbor lattice Z^2 and integer n>=1, the passage time from (0,0) to (n,0) equals the minimum over simple paths in the induced finite graph on [-2n,2n]^2 intersect Z^2. It lies between n and 2n. No iid or continuity hypothesis is needed. The reduction gives no fluctuation exponent.

rationale: The square endpoint refutes 'independence inferred solely from the iid input edges after global minimizing-path selection'; the route instead uses 'Refresh every edge independently at rate one' and an actual product-space covariance identity. The counterexample does not refute that valid identity.
from_statement: On a square with opposite terminals and four independent edge costs uniform on {1,2}, select the two-edge upper path when its total cost is no larger than the lower path. Given upper selection, the covariance of its successive edge costs is -5/121. Without conditioning, the covariance of the two selected edge costs is -9/256. Their total has variance 23/64, whereas the sum of their individual variances is 55/128. This finite example refutes independence inferred solely from the iid input edges after global minimizing-path selection; it gives no lattice fluctuation exponent.

to_statement: The campaign's P0104 record groups Questions 13 and 15 of Auffinger--Damron--Hanson's 50 years of first passage percolation (arXiv:1511.03262v2, PDF page 37): strict exponent below 1/2 in dimensions at least two under suitable edge-law conditions; exponent 1/3 in the plane; and a positive exponent in a suitable dimension. The source leaves suitable hypotheses and the exact variance-scaling convention to be specified. A bounded Uniform[1,2] planar variance-exponent attempt covers a restricted slice. The April 2026 arXiv:2604.01214v1 polynomial improvement is for its specified isotropic Riemannian continuum model and supplies no proved iid square-lattice transfer. October 2026 current openness is UNKNOWN under this targeted check, and no P0104 solution is claimed. Verified source hashes establish provenance, not mathematical proof.

rationale: The route explicitly uses 'L_n its first-order spectral limit, and R_n=H_n-L_n'; the lemma supplies 'Var(f)=L+integral_0^infinity exp(-t)R_f(t)dt'. This separation repairs the impossible full-unweighted-kernel envelope; the quantitative inputs remain unproved.
from_statement: For iid Uniform[1,2] undirected nearest-neighbor Z^2 FPP, T_n=T(0,n e1), let the UNWEIGHTED refresh kernel be H_n(t)=exp(t)(-C_n'(t)), L_n its first-order spectral limit, and R_n=H_n-L_n. A sufficient conditional route to variance comparable to n^(2/3) is: L_n<=C n^(2/3); R_n(t)<=C n F(n^(1/3)t) for every t>=0 with one nonnegative integrable F; and H_n(t)>=c n for 0<=t<=c' n^(-1/3). Constants are independent of n. The separated variance identity gives upper bound C n^(2/3)(1+integral F) and lower bound c c' exp(-c') n^(2/3). ALL THREE quantitative inputs remain unproved. The earlier all-time integrable envelope on the full unweighted H_n ignores a positive first-order floor and is infeasible; do not promote this corrected conditional route into a proof of its inputs or a solution of P0104.
to_statement: For a square-integrable function f of finitely many independent coordinates, let f_S be its orthogonal coordinate-average product projections. Refresh each coordinate independently at rate one, and set C_f(t)=Cov(f(W),f(W^t)), E_f(t)=-C_f'(t), and H_f(t)=exp(t)E_f(t). Then L=sum_{|S|=1}||f_S||_2^2 is the limit of H_f(t), R_f(t)=H_f(t)-L=sum_{|S|>=2}|S|exp(-(|S|-1)t)||f_S||_2^2 is nonnegative, and Var(f)=L+integral_0^infinity exp(-t)R_f(t)dt. If L>0, no bound H_f(t)<=A F(Bt) for all t>=0 can hold with finite positive A,B and a nonnegative integrable F. The weighted energy E_f itself tends to zero; the floor concerns the unweighted convention only.
